text:
incident-bot: Paging: SEV2 - sudden spike in 5xx/timeouts observed from prod-gateway in eu-west-1. Error rate up from ~0.3% to 8% over the last 6m, P50 latency unchanged, P95 increased ~2x. Auto-retry rate up. Pager: @oncall-sre @eng-runtime

Alice Chen: getting this alert now — seeing a dashboard spike too. Customers reporting 'timeout' from our hosted API.

Diego Torres: logs show a flood of `upstream reset` and `502` from the model-fetch service (model-router). Could be backend pool saturation.

Priya Singh: I'm on prod-gateway right now — tailing `gateway-access.log`. Lots of `504` and `upstream read timeout` at ~10:43:xx. No deploy in last 24h on gateway.

Jamal Ahmed: jumping in. Which regions are affected? eu-west-1 only or global?

Alice Chen: metric tag shows majority from eu-west-1, small blip in eu-central. us regions clean.

Mateo Rivera: checking model-router pool size; looks like a surge of large-sequence requests (seq_len > 1024) hitting a single routing shard. KV cache miss rates spiked.

Diego Torres: that aligns with the `upstream reset` — backend GPU workers are OOM'ing or getting overloaded, causing connection resets.

Priya Singh: I've temporarily bumped the router connection pool timeout to 120s in config to reduce immediate 504s — this is a stopgap.

Alice Chen: thanks. Can we put a circuit-breaker (503 fast-fail) in front of the overloaded shard to give it time to recover?

Jamal Ahmed: agreed — we should prevent head-of-line blocking. Oncall, can you patch a policy to route new large-seq requests to a fallback model variant in eu-west-2 or to the lower-cost shard?

Mateo Rivera: I can flip a routing flag for `large-seq-redirect` to prefer eu-west-2, but that will increase inter-region latency. Approving?

Priya Singh: do the customer impact assessment first — which customers are pinned to eu-west-1?

Alice Chen: customer list: acme-inc, medialabs, and two internal test accounts pinned to eu-west-1. Acme has ongoing batch jobs — likely to see failures.

Diego Torres: I'm pushing a temporary per-account rate-limit for non-SLA accounts to 10rps for the next 15m to reduce pressure.

incident-bot: Action log: `rate-limit` applied to account_group=non-sla at 10rps by Diego Torres.

Jamal Ahmed: good. Let's do these mitigations in parallel: 1) enable fallback routing for large seq to eu-west-2 (Mateo) 2) enforce temporary account rate-limits (Diego) 3) enable a short 503 fast-fail circuit on the hotspot shard (Priya/Alice)

Mateo Rivera: toggled `large-seq-redirect=true` in routing service; config propagated to 3/4 route nodes. Waiting on last node to converge.

Priya Singh: applying circuit-breaker rule now. `circuit_breaker: {consecutive_errors: 20, window: 30s, fallback: 503}` — deploying to 2 nodes first.

Alice Chen: I'm updating the oncall status and pinging SREs in eu-west-2 to watch increased CPU.

Diego Torres: rate-limit applied, seeing drop in inbound rps by ~18% to the hotspot. Error rate trending down to 3% now.

incident-bot: Metric update: error_rate from 8% -> 3.2% over 4m after mitigations.

Jamal Ahmed: that's promising. Who can do a quick heap/oom check on the GPU workers?

Mateo Rivera: running `kubectl top` and checking pod logs. I see repeated `alloc failed` in `model-worker-12` and `model-worker-15`. Restarting the two pods to free memory.

Priya Singh: restarted. Backpressure reduced, upstream errors decreased further.

Alice Chen: can we rollout a hotfix to the router to throttle oversized requests earlier (reject > 1200 tokens with 413)? We should prevent this class of requests from head-of-line blocking.

Diego Torres: we can push a small config update to do a soft-reject (429) for > 1200 token requests for non-SLA customers.

Jamal Ahmed: do it. Prioritize non-SLA soft-reject; SLA customers still allowed but routed to eu-west-2 fallback.

Mateo Rivera: updated router: `max_tokens_soft=1200` and `soft_reject_status=429` for account_group=non-sla. Propagated.

incident-bot: Note: change `max_tokens_soft` rolled to 4/4 router nodes.

Priya Singh: error rate holding ~1.1%, P95 still elevated but trending down. Customer complaints decreased.

Alice Chen: good. Turning incident to 'mitigated' — will transition to follow-up thread for root cause and action items. Anyone have evidence of config drift or recent change that could have triggered this?

Diego Torres: no deploys on gateway or router. The likely trigger: sudden customer workload shift (big sequences) + insufficient shard capacity + insufficient early-reject protection. This is more workload-profile than code bug.

Jamal Ahmed: agreed. For follow-up: we need a runbook update, alerts tuning, and a small hotfix to enforce early-reject for oversized requests. Also check autoscale thresholds for model-worker pools and consider prewarmed capacity for large-seq workloads.

Alice Chen: noted. I'll create action items and assign owners.

incident-bot: Creating follow-up checklist — items: [hotfix_router_early_reject, runbook_large_seq, alerts_p95_and_error_rate_thresholds, autoscale_review, customer_comms_draft] assigned by Alice Chen.

Mateo Rivera: I'll take `hotfix_router_early_reject` and `autoscale_review`. Diego you OK to take `alerts_p95_and_error_rate_thresholds`?

Diego Torres: yes taking alerts tuning. Priya can you own `runbook_large_seq` and `customer_comms_draft`?

Priya Singh: I'll draft the runbook updates and a short status email for Acme + Medialabs. Add SHIELD note for internal customers.

Jamal Ahmed: add a monitoring play to track `KV cache miss rate` and `large_seq_rate` with an alert when large_seq_rate > 2% of total for 5m. Also tune the error-rate alert to avoid fatigue: trigger at 4% sustained for 3m in a single region with supporting P95 increase.

Diego Torres: will update alerts. Suggest adding a `fast-fail` metric for shards that have >10% connection resets.

Alice Chen: customer impact: Acme batch job had ~12% of requests fail; we should offer to re-run or credit. Medialabs had intermittent errors but recovered. Drafting comms now.

incident-bot: Handoff: oncall SRE -> Jamal Ahmed (SRE Lead) at 1749999400.

Alice Chen: adding notes to incident tracker: root cause: workload-driven shard overload + lack of early-reject gating + autoscale sensitivity. Mitigation summary: routing fallback to eu-west-2, temporary rate-limits, circuit-breaker fast-fail, worker pod restarts, soft-reject for oversized requests.

Mateo Rivera: hotfix PR opened: `router: enforce early soft-reject and token-based throttling` -> awaiting review. I'll tag for priority merge.

Priya Singh: runbook draft: section 'large-sequence surges' — steps to identify, immediate mitigations (rate-limit, fallback routing, soft-reject), and recovery checks (pod OOMs, KV cache warm, P95 latency stable).

Diego Torres: alerts PR opened to lower noise and add new large_seq alert.

Jamal Ahmed: good. Next actions: 1) Merge hotfix and deploy to canary (Mateo) 2) Runbook review and push to docs (Priya) 3) Alerts tuning (Diego) 4) Customer comms (Alice) 5) Autoscale policy review (Mateo/Jamal). Targeting 24h for most follow-ups.

Alice Chen: minutes logged. I'll create the follow-up ticket and link this thread. If anyone sees regression, re-pager. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> follow-up. Ticket: INC-2026-4471 created and linked.

Mateo Rivera: small note — we'll also consider a long-term feature: predictive routing that detects sudden token-length distribution shifts and prewarms capacity. Adding to roadmap.

Priya Singh: thanks all. Closing active paging.

Diego Torres: +1. Closing thread and moving to postmortem workspace for write-up.

incident-bot: Thread closed at 1749999650.
